value.change_explanation: The known-True residence read is removed from the computational path: §152(c)(1) now distinguishes an expressly GIVEN legal intermediate from newly read interval endpoints and resolves the statutory more-than-half-year condition with inclusive calendar overlap. The same raw-observation/direct-GIVEN boundary is reused for the three newly acquired heads, while each wrapper selects only the temporal relation stated by its own source. Existing nonfocused behavior is otherwise preserved.

def surviving_spouse_death_timing_applies(facts):
    resolved = resolve_temporal_relation(
        facts.get('given_spouse_died_during_either_two_immediately_preceding_years'),
        'event_in_either_two_preceding_calendar_years',
        facts.get('query_year'),
        facts.get('spouse_date_of_death'),
        None,
        None,
        None,
        None)
    return {'value': resolved.get('value'), 'used_units': ['u2_a1A_death_timing_pred'], 'open_dependencies': resolved.get('open_dependencies', [])}

refinement_contracts.description: A shared pure resolver separates factual date perception from source-specific temporal resolution. Its callers select one of three source-backed relations: inclusive overlap exceeding half the calendar year, an event occurring in either of two immediately preceding calendar years, or the entire queried service interval falling within the stated status interval. Direct GIVEN branches remain available without reconstructing their antecedents.
refinement_contracts.name: raw_temporal_observation_resolution
observations: An expressly GIVEN temporal legal intermediate may be consumed directly, but a former derived neural boolean is not reused as that GIVEN.
Calendar residence is observed through explicit co-residence start and end dates plus the literal query year.
Death timing is observed through an explicit death date plus the literal taxable year.
Contemporaneous service/status rules are observed through explicit service and status interval endpoints.
Missing observations return an open dependency; invalid dates and reversed intervals raise rather than being fabricated or coerced.

unit_updates.property: whether the identified individual is the taxpayer's qualifying child
unit_updates.quote:
The term "qualifying child" means, with respect to any taxpayer for any taxable year, an individual-

        (A) who bears a relationship to the taxpayer described in paragraph (2),

        (B) who has the same principal place of abode as the taxpayer for more than one-half of such taxable year,

        (C) who meets the age requirements of paragraph (3), and

        (E) who has not filed a joint return (other than only for a claim of refund) with the individual's spouse for the taxable year beginning in the calendar year in which the taxable year of the taxpayer begins.
